blurb: Stocky, muscular American terrier the AKC calls confident, smart and good-natured
description: The American Staffordshire Terrier is a medium-sized, short-coated, muscular dog from the US, described by the AKC as confident, smart and good-natured.
answer: The American Staffordshire Terrier, or AmStaff, is a medium-sized, short-coated American breed descended from British bull-and-terrier dogs. It stands about 43–48 cm and weighs roughly 18–32 kg, and the AKC describes it as confident, smart and good-natured.

body: Bull-and-terrier dogs from the British Isles reached America from around 1850 and became the American Pit Bull Terrier, recognised by the United Kennel Club in 1898. The American Kennel Club recognised the breed in 1936 as the Staffordshire Terrier and renamed it American Staffordshire Terrier in 1969 to distinguish it from the British Staffordshire Bull Terrier.

Since the 1970s AmStaffs have been bred only from AKC-registered parents, and decades of selection for conformation have made them a distinct breed from the American Pit Bull Terrier. The breed is included in breed-specific legislation in a number of countries.

The AKC standard calls for great strength for its size: a stocky, muscular but agile dog, not long-legged or racy. Preferred heights are 46–48 cm for males and 43–46 cm for females. The head is medium-length with a broad skull and strong cheek muscles; ears may be cropped or uncropped, uncropped preferred. The nose is always black, and many short-coat colors are accepted, though liver, black and tan, and more than 80% white are discouraged.

The AKC describes AmStaffs as smart, confident, good-natured companions whose courage is proverbial, and says a responsibly bred, well-socialized dog is loyal and trustworthy. The breed club notes that aggression toward other dogs can occur even in well-socialized dogs, so they should not be left alone with other dogs.

Sources say little about routine care. As a strong, athletic dog with a short coat, it is generally thought to need regular exercise, early socialization and consistent training, and owners should check local laws that may restrict the breed.

A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years. Conditions reported in the breed include allergic skin disease, demodicosis, which one American study found in 20% of dogs under two, and hip and elbow dysplasia.

faq.q: How big does an American Staffordshire Terrier get?
faq.a: It stands about 43–48 cm at the shoulder and weighs roughly 18–32 kg, with males usually larger.

faq.q: Is an AmStaff the same as a Pit Bull?
faq.a: They share ancestry, but decades of separate breeding for conformation have made the AmStaff a distinct breed, typically stockier than the American Pit Bull Terrier.

faq.q: How long do American Staffordshire Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years for the breed.
